accuracy.evidence: Dates and facts checked against the Natural History Museum's Mary Anning pages and specimen notes, the Lyme Regis Museum and Torrens (1995, BJHS 28): born 1799 and died 1847 in Lyme Regis; Joseph found the ichthyosaur skull in 1811 and Mary the body in 1812 (she was 12 or 13, so 'about 12'); first complete plesiosaur 1823, which Cuvier first doubted; first pterosaur outside Germany 1828; dog Tray killed by a landslip 1833; Owen named Dinosauria in 1842 (30 years after 1812); the Geological Society admitted women from 1919; Royal Society 2010 list. Blue Lias is about 200 million years old (Jurassic Coast Trust). Ichthyosaurs had four paddles and a tail fin; belemnites are the bullet-shaped guards of squid-like animals.

misconceptions.evidence: Each step targets a documented slip: fossils can be dug out any time (tapping the bare beach before the storm says the fossils are still in the cliff; quiz tag storm, which also warns about cliff falls); the 1811 skull was a crocodile (step 2 prediction and quiz tag croc); her reptiles were dinosaurs (step 3 sort, step 4 date of the word, tag dino); a look-alike living animal means not extinct (step 5 matching, tag alive); she was welcomed by the scientific societies (tag credit).

lab_distinct.evidence: flaganning is built on this topic's own story and evidence: a Blue Lias cliff that only yields fossils after a storm, an ichthyosaur outline rebuilt from skull, backbone, paddles and tail fin with legs and wings rejected, a dinosaur or not sort of Mary's reptiles, a 1795-1850 line of time built from her finds against Owen's 1842 name, and fossil to living look-alike matching. It is not the coprolite lab or the fossils-as-evidence lab. Measured shingle overlap with any other flagship lab is at most 6%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Children discover each point before it is stated: the beach is empty until the storm, which is why Mary hunted after storms; the parts that fit the outline are paddles and a fin, so the animal swam; only the two land animals go in the Dinosaur box; the 1842 card lands far to the right of 1812 on the line; and every look-alike line ends with 'none is alive today'. The done line of each step then confirms the idea in one sentence.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'On a calm summer day' (the calm beach is bare), 'A crocodile' (the body has paddles and a tail fin), 'Yes, a swimming dinosaur' (it goes in Not a dinosaur, with the reason), and 'Yes, everyone said it' (the word arrives 30 years later on the line). A.reveal names the right answer after each task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions rotate; each wrong option carries a tag with its own message naming the slip: where (the beach below the Lyme Regis cliffs), dino (sea and flying reptiles are not dinosaurs), storm (storms expose fossils; never dig into the cliff), croc (the skeleton showed paddles and a tail fin), credit (women could not join the Geological Society) and alive (a look-alike is not the same animal).

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK grade 2.2 (family target 5.0) with short sentences, and names like ichthyosaur are always paired with plain words ('a sea reptile'). Adult text scores 5.9 (target 10). Lab banners are one short line each, with feedback lines of one or two sentences that name the reason.

no_filler.evidence: No phrases from the filler list. Every kid paragraph carries a fact needed later (place and date, why storms matter, the 1811 and 1812 finds, not dinosaurs and extinct, the credit problem). The adult paragraphs give sources, dates, mistakes and the lab plan with no repeated template text.

mobile.evidence: Checked at 390 px (iPhone 13 in the walk-through): the canvas switches to a taller 1.35 ratio, beach stones go to 3 columns, part cards to 3 columns, timeline cards to 2 columns and match rows stay in two columns; labels shrink to fit (never under 11 px) and every control is also a 44 px button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a matching button (Storm, Stone 1-6, each part, Dinosaur / Not a dinosaur, each year, each fossil and look-alike), each with a full aria-label. The canvas aria-label is updated with every feedback line and step description, and feedback is announced through c.say. axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) runs in both themes in the browser gate.
